elements.quote: Through an integrative review, we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes.

elements.quote: We assessed the methodological quality of studies using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool.

elements.quote: Following Whittemore and Knafl's methodological process: (1) problem identification; (2) literature search; (3) data evaluation; (4) data analysis; and (5) presentation

elements.quote: Of 18,783 articles retrieved, 64 fit the inclusion criteria. Qualitative designs were most commonly used for evaluation (48%), with individual interviews as the predominant data collection method.
elements.reason: The abstract reports the number of included studies and summarizes relevant study characteristics.

elements.quote: Of the 64 studies, 44% used a framework, 26% used a model, 11% used a tool, 5% used an instrument, and 14% used theory as their primary approach to evaluate sustainability. Most studies (77%) did not measure sustainability outcomes
elements.reason: The abstract presents main results with numbers of studies for each finding.

elements.quote: Of 18,783 articles retrieved, 64 fit the inclusion criteria.
elements.reason: No meta-analysis was conducted; this is a narrative/integrative synthesis of diverse study designs.

elements.quote: It is unclear which approach/approaches are most effective for evaluating sustainability

elements.quote: Our review offers methodological recommendations for sustainability evaluation research and highlights the importance in understanding mechanisms of sustainability to advance the field.
elements.reason: The abstract provides interpretation of the results and their implications.

elements.quote: There is limited evidence to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) for healthcare improvement.
elements.reason: The background describes the current state of knowledge, noting limited evidence on evaluating sustainability of EBIs, and the discussion further describes existing syntheses and knowledge gaps.

elements.quote: It is unclear which approach/approaches are most effective for evaluating sustainability and what measures and outcomes are most commonly used.
elements.reason: The importance and need for the review are explained: uncertainty about which approaches are effective for evaluating sustainability, and implementation is 'meaningless without long-term sustainability efforts.'

elements.quote: A focus on evaluation is what differentiates this review from recent syntheses published on approaches to sustainability research.
elements.reason: Similar reviews exist (e.g., Lennox et al. and other recent syntheses are cited) and the need for the current review is explained by its distinct focus on evaluation approaches.
This is a review of approaches used to evaluate sustainability, not a review of intervention effects, so describing a mechanism of action does not apply.
The review examines evaluation approaches for sustainability rather than assessing a specific complex intervention, so a logic model of intervention components is not required.

elements.quote: The aim of this integrative review was to identify and synthesize approaches that have been used to evaluate the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare. We aimed to enhance our understanding of sustainability definitions, research designs, data collection methods, timing, measures, and sustainability outcomes used for sustainability evaluation studies.
elements.reason: The review objectives are explicitly stated in a dedicated Aim section, also echoed in the abstract.

elements.quote: Integrative reviews can include diverse data sources and do not restrict the type of study design.
elements.reason: This is an integrative review of approaches to evaluating sustainability, not a review of intervention effects, so PICO-formatted planned comparisons do not apply.
